Bandwidth is not expensive, that is a myth. Suddenlink just upgraded the network in my area and will be offering 1 gig service for less than Google Fiber 1 gig. They still impose a mockery of a download cap though. The max possible bandwidth is the max possible bandwidth. The infrastructure doesn't grow arms and take cash from the wallets of the ISP employees because I'm streaming Netflix today, whereas I was just using Google+ and voat yesterday.

Oh, sorry I should have been more clear. I mean what the CDNs charge the distributors to host and send the files to the consumer.

I agree ISPs are full of crap about their costs.

Partially because that's what they have determined they can charge. Companies do a lot of research before sticking a price on their product in order to maximize their profits. Whatever mathematical voodoo they do has determined that they can charge more for a digital copy alone than for the BluRay. Part of that may be that lower income consumers prefer physical media (That's just a guess towards one pricing aspect).

Also, when estimating the base cost of a product a company includes every aspect of delivering that product to the consumer. This includes manufacturing, warehousing, and distribution. Companies have had time to streamline and integrate the physical distribution of physical media and it's easy to tack BlueRays onto that system (Less effort = Lower price). Digital delivery is somewhat new to many of these companies and requires that they tack on extra costs to allow existing systems to work. This is why you often see convenience fees when ordering some things online (e.g. tickets through Ticketmaster). They've tacked that on to the existing system to recover costs for new processes. Once these costs are in place they never seem to go away because the consumer is accustom to paying them.
